Anna: Quick heads-up: found a perf regression on the canary when we enabled mixed BF16/INT8 KV compaction. Profiling attached.
Kevin: ugh — what are the deltas?
Anna: p99 up ~+70% on longctx (24k tokens). Eviction rate spikes during burst windows. Short paste: 
```
kv_stats:
  evictions/s: baseline 9 -> canary 41
  hit_ratio: 0.88 -> 0.62
  p99_gen_latency(ms): 46 -> 79
  mem_used(GiB): 42 -> 36 (INT8 compaction)
kernel_selection:
  selected: int8_fused_attn -> fell back to generic_gemm at seq>2k
```
Devon: repro command I ran: `./bench --model=redwood/llama-13b --kv-precision=mixed --longctx=24000 --profile=kv,kernels`
Priya: are we quantizing per-slot or per-page? fragmentation could be killing reuse.
Anna: per-slot. We compress every slot including tiny metadata slots. Result: lots of small INT8 pages scattered -> scan/lookup overhead + TLB churn.
Lee: I saw kernel selector mis-score on A100: int8_fused_attn chosen then cost model flipped to fallback when seq > ~2k (est. memory-op budget exceeded).
Kevin: could we try hybrid: keep high-entropy slots BF16 and compress low-entropy ones to INT8? quick A/B.
Anna: did a tiny ablation: top-10% variance slots kept BF16 -> p99 down to ~52ms, hit_ratio 0.71, mem +7% versus canary.
Priya: that seems promising. We should formalize: variance threshold + minimum segment size (>256B) before compressing.
Devon: also note batching heuristics matter: batch packing that mixes long+short sequences made the selector choose the fallback more often.
Anna: flamegraph/upload: /tmp/flame-canary.svg (link) — shows lots of CPU in cache rewarm and memcpy hotspots after eviction.
ops-bot: deploy/canary-2026-03-17 rolled back (reason: perf-regression-kv-mix) :warning:
Lee: action for kernel team: add fast-path or update cost model for int8_fused_attn at seq>=2k so we avoid falling back unnecessarily.
Kevin: I'll open an RFC for `adaptive-precision-by-entropy` and cc Priya + Anna.
Priya: I'll schedule a nightly job to run mixed-precision longctx bench with per-slot variance logging + fragmentation stats.
Anna: tl;dr — INT8 compaction saves memory but fragmentation + small-slot compression + kernel fallbacks create a net perf loss for long-context workloads. Short-term mitigations: 1) entropy filter (keep top-N variance slots BF16), 2) never compress slots < 256B, 3) tweak kernel cost model and batching packer.
Devon: operational guard idea: if evictions/s > 20 and p99 > 60ms during canary, auto-snapshot and rollback.
Kevin: noted — opening issue and assigning next steps.
Anna: thanks — will attach the profiler traces and a minimal reproducer in the issue.
